chains.title: TCF7L2 occupies the ref allele at an 8q24 pELS and may regulate MYC, but allele specificity is unproven

links.claim: TCF7L2 is the best HCT116-occupied candidate TF at this base, with ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks over the variant in HCT116 and expression at 63.61 TPM. QBiC-SELEX gives ref T > alt C for its CIS-BP-mapped TCF7 model (z = -8.8, effect = -0.429), but the k-mer site is weak (ref 90.0th, alt 87.2th percentile), so the ChIP peak may reflect another site in the element and allele-specific binding at this base is not established.
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

A candidate target is MYC, which is 334.2 kb upstream at 8q24 and has locus biology linked to colorectal cancer. This is proximity/biological inference only: the GTEx eQTL lookup is null and L2G instead favors POU5F1B, so the variant-to-MYC regulatory link is weak.
HCT116 is a colorectal cancer cell line in which TCF7L2 is expressed and ENCODE ChIP-seq has a peak over this variant, making it the relevant expression context.

A colorectal cancer connection is plausible through Wnt/TCF7L2-MYC biology, but direct variant-disease evidence is absent: there are no GWAS Catalog associations for this variant, no significant GTEx colon eQTL, and the provided L2G credible sets are not colorectal cancer.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP in HCT116 at this base should show higher ref T occupancy than alt C if M1 is correct.
An allele-specific enhancer reporter in HCT116 should show a TCF7L2-dependent decrease for alt C relative to ref T if TCF7L2 activates the element.
TCF7L2 knockdown or CRISPR disruption of the enhancer should reduce any allele-dependent MYC expression effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP in HCT116 does not show higher TCF7L2 occupancy on ref T than alt C at this base.
An allele-specific enhancer reporter in HCT116 does not show a TCF7L2-dependent difference between ref T and alt C.
TCF7L2 knockdown or enhancer disruption does not attenuate any allele-dependent enhancer or MYC expression effect.

chains.title: NFIC binds the alt allele strongly in vitro but lacks HCT116 occupancy evidence

links.claim: NFIC has a strong QBiC-SELEX alt C > ref T effect (z = 24.28, effect = +1.783; strong site, ref 96.3th and alt 99.5th percentile) and is expressed in HCT116 at 36.29 TPM. However, ENCODE ChIP-seq occupancy over this variant is reported only in HepG2, not HCT116, and NFIA shares the same mapped NFIB model and identical QBiC-SELEX statistics, so NFIC is chosen over NFIA mainly by expression and the relevant-cell occupancy evidence is missing.
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

POU5F1B is the best L2G gene at this locus (score 0.83) and is 79.1 kb from the variant, but the credible sets are for PSA and urinary incontinence rather than colorectal cancer and direct NFIC regulation of POU5F1B is not shown.
HCT116 expresses NFIC, but the provided ENCODE ChIP data do not show NFIC occupancy over this variant in HCT116; occupancy is only in HepG2.
POU5F1B is linked to colorectal cancer in the provided literature and L2G data, but no evidence ties this specific NFIC-binding allele to colorectal cancer.

predictions: If NFIC acts here, alt C should increase NFIC occupancy in HCT116 at this base and, if NFIC is an activator, increase POU5F1B expression.
NFIC knockdown should reduce any alt-C-dependent enhancer or POU5F1B expression effect in HCT116.
The allele-dependent effect should be absent in cell types where NFIC does not occupy this element.
falsified_if: Alt C does not increase NFIC occupancy in HCT116 at this base.
NFIC knockdown does not reduce any alt-C-dependent enhancer or POU5F1B expression effect in HCT116.
The allele-dependent effect is present in cell types where NFIC does not occupy this element.

chains.title: SP1 occupies the ref allele at the pELS and may regulate CCAT2, but allele specificity and target regulation are unproven

links.claim: SP1 is expressed in HCT116 and has ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks over the variant in HCT116. QBiC-SELEX gives ref T > alt C for its best CIS-BP-mapped SP3 model (z = -7.07, effect = -0.298), but the k-mer site is weak (ref 90.4th, alt 75.6th percentile), so occupancy could reflect another site in the element and allele-specific binding at this base is not established.
The variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

A candidate target is CCAT2 because the variant lies in a CCAT2 non_coding_transcript_exon and the cCRE is annotated near CCAT2. There is no direct evidence that this variant regulates CCAT2 or that SP1 mediates such regulation.
HCT116 is a colorectal cancer cell line in which SP1 is expressed and ENCODE ChIP-seq has a peak over this variant.

The CCAT2 colorectal cancer connection is indirect in the provided data. There are no GWAS associations for this variant, no significant GTEx colon eQTL, and the cited literature discusses CCAT2 mainly in gastrointestinal cancer rather than this variant in colorectal cancer.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401265:T>C, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 40 occupied (6 with a strong site), 5 of 103 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 11 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 517 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 5 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
